claim_withdrawn: Prefill is flat / never improves at any length
why_wrong: Read the 62k point as the general case; it was one point on a non-monotonic curve.
Compared arms against a baseline measured in an EARLIER, faster session window (~10% drift).
correction: With the baseline interleaved: combo is 1.157x FASTER at 130k.

claim_withdrawn: 130k is inconclusive (11.2% spread exceeds the effect)
why_wrong: Correct observation, wrong diagnosis -- blamed boot-to-boot noise. Real consecutive-boot drift is 0.07%; the gap was SESSION drift.
correction: n=4 resolved it; and the reference had to be re-measured in-window.

claim_withdrawn: EXL3_MOE_CPU_THREADS=16 is separable and safe alone, a pure decode win at every length
correction: It IS decode-only (prefill unchanged) but worth only 1.026x at 130k; mcs380 carries the long-context win.

claim_withdrawn: The 224k prefill win comes from KV-cache pressure pushing CPU MoE work into the prefill path
correction: mcs380 speeds prefill +14% at 130k where the cache is only ~50% full. No paging story needed.

claim_withdrawn: MTP acceptance tracks intrinsic token predictability; code is the most predictable case
why_wrong: Asserted a mechanism with no measurement, on a contested premise.
correction: Measured acceptance: curl 75.4% > code 68.7% > prose 61.0%. Code is NOT the best case.

claim_withdrawn: The config.yml md5 invariant was vacuous (0fe01cc8 = the combo config)
why_wrong: Misread a backup filename as an applied config.
correction: config.yml.kb-<arm> is the PRISTINE snapshot taken BEFORE that arm ran. The invariant was valid all along.

claim_withdrawn: 250k is bimodal: 1.134x or 1.016x depending on the boot
why_wrong: Compared combo's FAST machine state against baseline's NORMAL state.
correction: Both arms enter the state. Matched within state: 1.011x slow / 0.978x fast = PARITY.

claim_withdrawn: Pagefile reads correlate with the 250k fast/slow mode
why_wrong: Time window misaligned: jsonl ts is written at END of run, so the window captured post-run teardown.
correction: Anchored to the real sustained window: 2 of 3 SLOW boots had near-zero reads while the FAST boot had the third-highest.

claim_withdrawn: ndt6 beating ndt5 on both axes means the knob is still rising, sweep up
why_wrong: Treated two axes moving together as a trend signal; acceptance is not the objective.
correction: Swept 3-10: acceptance rises monotonically but speed peaks at ndt3 (+7.2%) and decays past ndt6.

claim_withdrawn: 'mcs380 is the only viable value' / '405 is backwards'
why_wrong: Overstated: 390/405 were measured offline but NEVER live-booted. And the direction claim was right.
correction: 375 tested live: boots, 0.3% gain (noise). 380 stands as the measured floor.
